leads.title: Ohio Senate Bill 104
leads.documents: Bans transgender students from using sex-segregated bathrooms, locker rooms, and overnight accommodations; allows single-occupancy restroom exception
leads.detail: Signed by Governor Mike DeWine on November 27, 2024; also contains college-credit legislation, noted as possible single-subject violation; opposed by ACLU of Ohio and Equality Ohio

leads.title: Ohio House Bill 8 - Schools parental notification law
leads.documents: Requires educators/counselors to out LGBTQ students to parents; bans 'sexual content' including 'gender ideology' K-3 and mandates opt-out provisions
leads.detail: Signed by Governor DeWine January 8, 2025; vast majority of public testimony opposed

leads.title: Ohio HB68 - Saving Adolescents from Experimentation (SAFE) Act
leads.documents: Bans gender-affirming puberty blockers, hormones, and surgery for under-18; bans transgender girls/women from women's high school and college sports teams
leads.detail: Passed Dec 13, 2023; vetoed Dec 29, 2023 by Gov. DeWine; veto overridden by House Jan 10, 2024 and Senate Jan 24, 2024; blocked April 2024, allowed Aug 2024, injunction reinstated March 18, 2025 by 10th District Court of Appeals, AG Dave Yost vowed appeal

leads.title: Ray v. McCloud
leads.documents: Federal ruling invalidating Ohio's ban on amending gender marker on birth certificates as unconstitutional
leads.detail: Decided December 2020 by federal judge Michael H. Watson; Ohio Department of Health did not appeal; effective June 1, 2021 transgender individuals allowed to update birth certificate; filed March 2018 by four transgender Ohioans with ACLU and Lambda Legal support

leads.title: In re Ladrach (1987)
leads.documents: Prior Ohio court precedent prohibiting amendment of gender marker on birth certificate after sex reassignment surgery
leads.detail: 1987 court case cited as basis for ban until revised 2016 and overruled by Ray v. McCloud; left Ohio as one of three states banning corrections at time of 2018 lawsuit

leads.title: Ohio Bureau of Motor Vehicles - Declaration of Gender Change / 2026 marker policy
leads.documents: Procedures for changing name/gender on driver's license/ID; history of X marker and 2026 rollback to M/F only with matching birth certificate/passport
leads.detail: Requires court order for name and Declaration of Gender Change signed by physician, nurse practitioner, social worker, therapist or psychologist; X option since April 2022; August 2026 BMV announced male-or-female-only rule requiring exact matching sex/name

leads.title: U.S. Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit - March 7, 2018 transgender employment ruling
leads.documents: Held discrimination on basis of transgender status is discrimination on basis of 'sex' under Title VII; employers may not use Religious Freedom Restoration Act to justify anti-LGBTQ discrimination
leads.detail: Covers Kentucky, Michigan, Ohio, Tennessee; case of Aimee Stephens, transgender woman fired in 2013 after disclosing transition at funeral home; appealed as R.G. & G.R. Harris Funeral Homes Inc. v. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission

leads.title: Bostock v. Clayton County / R.G. & G.R. Harris Funeral Homes Inc. v. EEOC
leads.documents: U.S. Supreme Court establishment that workplace discrimination on basis of sexual orientation or gender identity is sex discrimination under Title VII
leads.detail: Decided June 15, 2020; heard 2019 term concurrently with Altitude Express, Inc. v. Zarda; cited as basis for LGBTQ employment illegality in Ohio

leads.title: Ohio Governor Executive Orders on state employment (Kasich 2011, 2018)
leads.documents: Prohibition of sexual orientation and gender identity discrimination in state employment where statutes are silent
leads.detail: Executive order Jan 21, 2011 covering sexual orientation; new order Dec 19, 2018 adding gender identity or expression; Ohio statutes do not address sexual orientation/gender identity discrimination generally

leads.title: Human Rights Campaign State Rating - January 2023 / Movement Advancement Project
leads.documents: Institutional assessments of Ohio LGBTQ equality infrastructure and conversion-therapy bans
leads.detail: HRC gave Ohio 'High Priority to Achieve Basic Equality' Jan 2023, noted Ohio cities as leaders in LGBTQ-friendly policy; MAP notes no state conversion-therapy law, seven cities banned (Cincinnati Dec 2015, Toledo/Columbus/Dayton/Athens 2017, Lakewood/Kent 2018, Cleveland/Cleveland Heights/Akron/Reynoldsburg 2022)
